3 - [[Anne McLean]] (translator)|website={{URL|www.dublinliteraryaward.ie}}}} The '''Dublin Literary Award''' ({{langx|ga|Gradam Liteartha Idirnáisiúnta Bhaile Átha Cliath}}), established as the '''International IMPAC Dublin Literary Award''' in 1996 and known as the '''International Dublin Literary Award''' (2016–2020), is presented each year for a novel written or translated into English. It promotes excellence in world literature and is solely sponsored by [[Dublin City Council]], Ireland. At [[Euro|€]]100,000, the award is one of the [[List of richest literary prizes|richest literary prizes in the world]]. If the winning book is a translation (as it has been twelve times), the prize is divided between the writer and the translator, with the writer receiving €75,000 and the translator €25,000.{{cite news|url=http://www.dutchnews.nl/news/archives/2010/06/dutch_writer_wins_worlds_bigge.php|title=Dutch writer wins world's biggest literature prize|date=18 June 2010|work=DutchNews.nl|access-date=18 June 2010|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100619150849/http://www.dutchnews.nl/news/archives/2010/06/dutch_writer_wins_worlds_bigge.php|archive-date=19 June 2010}} The first award was made in 1996 to [[David Malouf]] for his English-language novel ''[[Remembering Babylon]]''.{{Cite news |last=Battersby |first=Eileen |author-link=Eileen Battersby |date=17 June 1996 |title=Malouf wins first Impac literary award |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/malouf-wins-first-impac-literary-award-1.59034 |access-date=22 June 2017 |newspaper=The Irish Times |archive-date=24 July 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170724150531/http://www.irishtimes.com/news/malouf-wins-first-impac-literary-award-1.59034 |url-status=live }} Nominations are submitted by [[public library|public libraries]] worldwide – over 400 library systems in 177 countries worldwide are invited to nominate books each year – from which the shortlist and the eventual winner are selected by an international panel of judges (which changes each year).{{Cite web |date=2025-10-17 |title=Dublin's international literary award: how a global network of 400 libraries contributes |url=https://worldcitiescultureforum.com/city-project/dublin-literary-award-establishing-an-international-network/ |access-date=2025-11-13 |website=World Cities Culture Forum |language=en-US}} ==Eligibility and procedure== The prize is open to novels written in any language and by authors of any nationality, provided the work has been published in English or English translation. The presentation of the award is post-dated by two years from the date of publication. Thus, to win an award in 2017, the work must have been published in 2015. If it is an English translation, the work must have been published in its original language between two and six years before its translation.{{Cite web| url= http://www.dublinliteraryaward.ie/faqs/| publisher= Dublin City Public Libraries| access-date= 25 July 2017| title= FAQs| archive-date= 22 November 2015| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20151122230914/http://www.dublinliteraryaward.ie/faqs/| url-status= dead}} The scope for inclusion has been subject to criticism; according to ''[[The Irish Times]]'' journalist [[Eileen Battersby]], "many of the titles are already well known even at the time of the publication of the long list."{{cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/culture/books/jos%C3%A9-eduardo-agualusa-wins-100-000-international-dublin-literary-award-1.3127773|title=José Eduardo Agualusa wins €100,000 International Dublin Literary Award|last1=Battersby|first1=Eileen|date=21 June 2017|newspaper=The Irish Times|access-date=21 June 2017|archive-date=23 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211023123925/https://www.irishtimes.com/culture/books/jos%C3%A9-eduardo-agualusa-wins-100-000-international-dublin-literary-award-1.3127773|url-status=live}} [[Dublin City Public Libraries and Archive|Dublin City Public Libraries]] seek nominations from 400 [[Public library|public libraries]] from major cities across the world. Libraries can apply to be considered for inclusion in the nomination process.{{Cite web | url = http://www.dublinliteraryaward.ie/libraries-2017/ | title = Libraries 2017 | publisher = Dublin City Public Libraries | access-date = 25 July 2017 | archive-date = 26 July 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170726233158/http://www.dublinliteraryaward.ie/libraries-2017/ | url-status = live }} The longlist is announced in October or November of each year, and the shortlist (up to 10 titles) is announced in March or April of the following year. The longlist and shortlist are chosen by an international panel of judges which rotates each year. [[Allen Weinstein]] was the non-voting chair of the panel from 1996 to 2003. As of 2017, the former Chief Judge of the US Court of Appeals, [[Eugene R. Sullivan]], is the non-voting chair.{{Cite web | url = http://www.dublinliteraryaward.ie/2017-judging-panel/ | title = 2017 Judging Panel | publisher = Dublin City Public Libraries | access-date = 26 July 2017 | archive-date = 31 July 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170731093421/http://www.dublinliteraryaward.ie/2017-judging-panel/ | url-status = live }} The winner of the award is announced each June. ==History== The award was established in 1994 as the '''International IMPAC Dublin Literary Award''', a joint initiative of [[Dublin City Council]] and the American productivity company IMPAC, which had its European headquarters in Dublin. James Irwin, president of IMPAC, established the prize money at €100,000. A trust fund was established to pay for the award and its maintenance. The award has been administered by Dublin City Public Libraries since its inception. IMPAC went defunct in the late-2000s when its founder and president James Irwin died in 2009. In late 2013, the trust fund became exhausted and there was no money left to run the award. The council agreed to step in and continue funding the award under the same brand name of the now-defunct company while seeking a new sponsor.{{cite news|newspaper=The Irish Times|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/culture/new-sponsor-sought-for-100-000-impac-literary-award-1.2232674|title=New sponsor sought for €100,000 Impac literary Award|last=Hilliard|first=Mark|date=31 May 2015|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150718232658/http://www.irishtimes.com/culture/new-sponsor-sought-for-100-000-impac-literary-award-1.2232674|archive-date=18 July 2015}} It was reported that the council paid €100,000 for the prize plus €80,250 in administration costs in 2015. The award was subsequently renamed the International DUBLIN Literary Award in November 2015.{{cite web | title=About | url=https://dublinliteraryaward.ie/about/ }} In 2021, it was awarded as the Dublin Literary Award.{{cite news | title=Valeria Luiselli wins €100,000 Dublin Literary Award for Lost Children Archive | newspaper=[[The Irish Times]] | url=https://www.irishtimes.com/culture/books/valeria-luiselli-wins-100-000-dublin-literary-award-for-lost-children-archive-1.4570273 }} Describing the award as "the most eclectic and unpredictable of the literary world's annual gongs", the journalist Michelle Pauli posed the question in relation to the longlist for the 2004 edition: "Where would you find [[Michael Dobbs]] and [[Tony Parsons (British journalist)|Tony Parsons]] up against [[Umberto Eco]] and [[Milan Kundera]] for a €100,000 prize?"{{cite news|first=Michelle|last=Pauli|url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2003/nov/18/news.impacprize?INTCMP=ILCNETTXT3487|title=Bestsellers make impact on eclectic longlist|work=The Guardian|date=18 November 2003|access-date=18 November 2003|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140715090333/http://www.theguardian.com/books/2003/nov/18/news.impacprize?INTCMP=ILCNETTXT3487|archive-date=15 July 2014}} ===Winners and shortlists=== ==== 1990s ==== {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible" |+Dublin Literary Award winners and finalists, 1996–1999 !Year !Author !Title !Result !Ref. |-style=background:#cddeff ! rowspan="7" |[[1996 in literature|1996]] |{{sortname|last=Malouf|first=David}} |''[[Remembering Babylon]]'' |Winner | |- |{{sortname|last=Banville|first=John}} |''[[Ghosts (Banville novel)|Ghosts]]'' |Shortlist | |- |{{sortname|last=Naipaul|first=V.
